styloid process of temporal bone: Thin process projecting downwards below the ear; three 'stylo-' muscles and two ligaments attach to it.
styloid process of third metacarpal bone: Small process on the base of the 3rd metacarpal; the ECRB tendon attaches near it.
stylomandibular ligament: Ligament from the styloid process to the angle of the mandible; separates the parotid and submandibular glands.
stylopharyngeus muscle: The only muscle supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX); it raises the pharynx and larynx during swallowing.
subacromial bursa: Between the acromion and the supraspinatus tendon; it becomes inflamed in impingement syndrome and is used for injections.
subclavius muscle: Runs from the 1st rib to the lower surface of the clavicle; protects the neurovascular structures beneath in clavicle fractures. Nerve to subclavius.
subcutaneous acromial bursa: Under the skin over the acromion.
subcutaneous bursa of lateral malleolus: Bursa under the skin over the lateral ankle prominence.
subcutaneous bursa of medial malleolus: Bursa under the skin over the medial ankle prominence.
subcutaneous bursa of tuberosity of tibi: Subcutaneous bursa in front of the tibial tuberosity.
subcutaneous calcaneal bursa: Between the Achilles tendon and the skin; it becomes inflamed from shoe friction.
subcutaneous infrapatellar bursa: Under the skin in front of the patellar ligament; it becomes inflamed in people who work kneeling.
subcutaneous prepatellar bursa: Subcutaneous bursa in front of the patella; its inflammation is known as 'housemaid's knee'.
subcutaneous trochanteric bursa: Under the skin over the greater trochanter.
subdeltoid bursa: Between deltoid and the humeral head; usually continuous with the subacromial bursa.
subfacial prepatellar bursa: Bursa in front of the patella beneath the fascia.
sublime tubercle: Prominence on the medial side of the coronoid process; the anterior band of the ulnar collateral ligament attaches to it.
sublingual fossa: Fossa on the inner surface above the mylohyoid line; the sublingual gland lies in it.
subscapular fossa: Anterior surface facing the chest wall; subscapularis arises here.
subscapularis muscle: Rotator cuff muscle filling the front of the scapula; inserts into the lesser tubercle and rotates the arm medially. Subscapular nerves.
subtendinous bursa of iliacus muscle: Between the iliopsoas tendon and the lesser trochanter.
subtendinous bursa of infraspinatus musc: Between the infraspinatus tendon and the capsule.
subtendinous bursa of obturator internus: Between the tendon and the hip capsule.
subtendinous bursa of sartorius muscle: Between the sartorius tendon and the other pes anserinus tendons.
subtendinous bursa of teres major muscle: Between the teres major tendon and the humerus.
subtendinous bursa of tibialis anterior: Between the tibialis anterior tendon and the medial cuneiform.
subtendinous bursa of trapezius muscle: Between the ascending part of trapezius and the spine of the scapula.
subtendinous bursa of triceps brachii mu: Between the triceps tendon and the olecranon.
subtendinous calcaneal bursa: Between the Achilles tendon and the back of the calcaneus (retrocalcaneal bursa); it becomes inflamed in Haglund's deformity.
subtendinous prepatellar bursa: Between the quadriceps tendon and the patella.
sulcus of auditory tube: Groove in which the cartilaginous part of the auditory (Eustachian) tube lies.
superficial head of flexor pollicis brev: Superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis
Arises from the flexor retinaculum; supplied by the median nerve.
superficial head of pronator teres: Arises from the medial epicondyle; the median nerve passes between the two heads and can be compressed here (pronator syndrome).
superficial investing cervical fascia: Investing layer of deep cervical fascia
Fascial layer surrounding the neck and enclosing sternocleidomastoid and trapezius like a sheath.
superficial layer of temporal fascia: Layer of the strong fascia covering temporalis that attaches to the outer lip of the zygomatic arch.
superficial part of anterior compartment: Superficial layer of anterior forearm compartment
superficial part of masseter: Powerful masticatory fibres from the zygomatic arch to the angle of the mandible; masseteric nerve (V3). It closes the jaw.
superficial part of posterior compartmen: Superficial layer of posterior forearm compartment
Superficial layer of posterior leg compartment
superficial part of tibial collateral li: Superficial part of medial collateral ligament
Flat band from the medial epicondyle to the shaft of the tibia; resists valgus stress.
superficial transverse metacarpal ligame: Transverse fibres at the bases of the fingers in the palm.
superficial transverse metatarsal ligame: Transverse fibres of the plantar aponeurosis at the bases of the toes.
superior angle of scapula: Superomedial angle of the scapula; levator scapulae attaches to it.
superior articular facet of vertebra: Surface of the superior articular process that forms a facet joint.
superior articular process of sacrum: Process forming a facet joint with L5.
superior articular process of vertebra: Process that articulates with the vertebra above.
superior articular surface of atlas: Concavity on the upper surface of the lateral mass; with the occipital condyles it forms the joint for the 'yes' movement.
superior articular surface of lateral co: Superior articular surface of lateral condyle
Surface of the lateral condyle that articulates with the femur.
superior articular surfaces of tibia: Surfaces of the tibial plateau that articulate with the femoral condyles.
superior border of scapula: Short upper border of the scapula; the inferior belly of omohyoid arises here.
superior bursa of biceps femoris muscle: At the origin of the long head of biceps femoris.
superior costal facet: Half facet on the upper border of the body; articulates with the head of the rib of the same number.
superior extensor retinaculum of ankle: Transverse band in front of the ankle holding the extensor tendons.
superior facet of talus: Superior facet of trochlea of talus
Upper articular surface of the trochlea facing the tibia.
superior fibular retinaculum: Band holding the fibular tendons behind the lateral malleolus; when it tears the tendons dislocate.
superior gemellus muscle: Runs from the ischial spine to join the obturator internus tendon; a lateral rotator.
superior glenohumeral ligament: Thin ligament on the inner surface of the capsule; limits inferior translation with the arm at the side.
